hindi: अब इसके बाद हम त्रिशोथीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the three swellings (Triśothīya).
notes: Prose opening formula of the chapter; the unit is typed as a verse in the input but is a prose line.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula; ha and sma are particles, not rendered separately.

hindi: शोथ तीन होते हैं, जो वात, पित्त और कफ के कारण होते हैं; वे फिर निज और आगन्तु भेद से दो प्रकार के होते हैं।
english: There are three swellings (śotha), caused by Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman); they, again, are of two kinds by the division into endogenous (nija) and exogenous (āgantu).

hindi: उनमें आगन्तु शोथ काटने, भेदने, घाव लगने, तोड़ने, कुचलने, पीसने, प्रहार, वध, बाँधने, लपेटने, बेधने, दबाने आदि से; या भल्लातक के फूल, फल और रस, आत्मगुप्ता के शूक, शूकयुक्त कृमि तथा अहितकर पत्तों, लताओं और गुल्मों के स्पर्श से; या विषैले प्राणियों के पसीने, ऊपर रेंगने और मूत्र करने से; या विषयुक्त प्राणियों की दाढ़ों, दाँतों, सींगों और नखों के आघात से; या समुद्र के विष, वायु, हिम और अग्नि के स्पर्श से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: Among these, the exogenous swellings arise from cutting, splitting, wounding, breaking, crushing, pounding, striking, beating (vadha), binding, wrapping, piercing, pressing and the like; or from contact with the flower, fruit and juice of bhallātaka, the bristles of ātmaguptā, bristly worms (krimiśūka), and harmful leaves, creepers and shrubs; or from the sweat, crawling over and urinating of poisonous creatures; or from the strokes of the fangs, teeth, horns and nails of venomous creatures; or from contact with sea-poison, wind, frost and fire.

text_flags.why: saṃṣṭrā is not a word; daṃṣṭrā (fang) fits the list of biting and striking parts (teeth, horns, nails)

notes: viṣiṇām (of poisonous creatures) is read with the preceding sweat, crawling and urine. vadha literally 'striking, killing', here among injuries; rendered 'beating'. sāgaraviṣa is read as 'poison of the sea'; it could also be taken with vāta as 'poisonous sea-wind'. Plant identifications (standard): bhallātaka = Semecarpus anacardium; ātmaguptā = Mucuna pruriens. krimiśūka is taken as 'bristly worm (caterpillar)'.

hindi: वे फिर आरम्भ में अपने-अपने कारणों और लक्षणों से पहचाने जाते हैं, जो निज शोथ के लक्षणों से अंशतः विपरीत होते हैं; और बन्धन, मन्त्र, अगद, प्रलेप, प्रताप, निर्वापण आदि उपक्रमों से उपचार किए जाने पर वे शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: They, again, are recognised at the outset by their respective causes and signs, which differ in part from the signs of the endogenous [swellings]; and, being treated with measures such as bandaging, incantations, antidotes (agada), smearing (pralepa), heating and cooling (nirvāpaṇa), they subside.

text_flags.why: vyañjnaiḥ is not a form; vyañjana (sign) as in nijavyañjana in the same unit

notes: nijavyañjanaikadeśaviparītaiḥ is read as qualifying hetuvyañjanaiḥ: the signs of exogenous swellings are partly contrary to those of the endogenous. Grammatically nijavyañjanaikadeśaviparītaiḥ could also qualify upakramaiḥ ('with measures partly contrary to the signs of the endogenous').

hindi: निज शोथ फिर स्नेहन, स्वेदन, वमन, विरेचन, आस्थापन, अनुवासन और शिरोविरेचन के अनुचित प्रयोग से, या मिथ्या संसर्जन से; या छर्दि, अलसक, विसूचिका, श्वास, कास, अतिसार, शोष, पाण्डुरोग, उदर, ज्वर, प्रदर, भगन्दर और अर्श रोगों से हुई अत्यधिक कृशता से; या कुष्ठ, कण्डू, पिडका आदि से; या छर्दि, छींक, डकार, शुक्र, अधोवायु, मूत्र और मल के वेगों को रोकने से; या कर्म, रोग, उपवास और मार्ग चलने से कृश हुए व्यक्ति द्वारा सहसा अति गुरु, अम्ल, लवण, पिष्टान्न, फल, शाक, राग, दही, हरितक, मद्य, मन्दक, विरूढ, नए शूकधान्य और शमीधान्य, तथा आनूप और औदक मांस के सेवन से; मिट्टी, कीचड़ और ढेले खाने से; अधिक लवण खाने से; गर्भ के दबाव से; आम गर्भ के गिरने से; और प्रसूता स्त्रियों में मिथ्या उपचार से तथा दोषों के उदीर्ण होने से उत्पन्न होते हैं। इस प्रकार सामान्य हेतु कहा गया।
english: The endogenous ones, again, arise from improper administration of oleation, sweating, emesis, purgation, decoction enema, unctuous enema and head-evacuation, or from a faulty graded diet (saṃsarjana); or from excessive emaciation due to the disorders vomiting, alasaka, visūcikā, dyspnoea, cough, diarrhoea, wasting (śoṣa), pāṇḍu disease, udara, fever, pradara, bhagandara and arśas; or from kuṣṭha, itching, pimples (piḍakā) and the like; or from suppression of the urges of vomiting, sneezing, belching, semen, flatus, urine and faeces; or, in one emaciated by action (karma), disease, fasting or travel, from the sudden excessive use of heavy, sour and salty things, flour-foods, fruits, vegetables, rāga, curd, green herbs, wine, mandaka, sprouted grain, new awned grain and pod grain, and the flesh of marsh and aquatic animals; from eating clay, mud or clods; from eating too much salt; from pressure of the foetus; from the falling of an unformed foetus; and, in women who have given birth, from wrong care and from the aggravated state of the doṣas. Thus the general cause has been stated.

text_flags.why: paṅka (mud) has the velar nasal before k; paṇka is not a word
possible: sāpīḍana is no regular formation; saṃpīḍana (pressure) gives the sense

notes: karma here is rendered 'action'; it may refer to the therapeutic procedures listed at the start of the unit. ati- is read as governing the whole list of foods (excessive use); it may qualify only guru. sahasā is read with the list of foods. udīrṇadoṣatvāt may belong only to the women after delivery or be a separate general cause. śotha and śopha are used interchangeably (both 'swelling'). Disease names (alasaka, visūcikā, pāṇḍu, udara, pradara, bhagandara, arśas, kuṣṭha) and the foods rāga and mandaka are kept in Sanskrit. -arśovikārātikarśanaiḥ may also be read as a dvandva: 'by the disorders vomiting ... arśas, or by excessive emaciation'. karma could also mean physical work.
lines_deva: निजाः पुनः स्नेहस्वेदवमनविरेचनास्थापनानुवासनशिरोविरेचनानामयथावत्प्रयोगान्मिथ्यासंसर्जनाद्वा छर्द्यलसकविसूचिकाश्वासकासातिसारशोषपाण्डुरोगोदरज्वरप्रदरभगन्दरार्शोविकारातिकर्शनैर्वा कुष्ठकण्डूपिडकादिभिर्वा छर्दिक्षवथूद्गारशुक्रवातमूत्रपुरीषवेगधारणैर्वा कर्मरोगोपवासाध्वकर्शितस्य वा सहसातिगुर्वम्ललवणपिष्टान्नफलशाकरागदधिहरितकमद्यमन्दकविरूढनवशूकशमीधान्यानूपौदकपिशितोपयोगान्मृत्पण्कलोष्टभक्षणाल्लवणातिभक्षणाद्गर्भसापीडनादामगर्भप्रपतनात् प्रजातानां च मिथ्योपचारादुदीर्णदोषत्वाच्च शोफाः प्रादुर्भवन्ति इत्युक्तः सामान्यो हेतुः

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past pass. part. ava-√lip, tat-puruṣa

hindi: किन्तु यहाँ यह विशेषता है: शीत, रूक्ष, लघु, विशद पदार्थों, श्रम, उपवास, अति कर्शन, क्षपण आदि से कुपित वायु त्वचा, मांस, रक्त आदि को अभिभूत करके शोफ उत्पन्न करता है। वह शीघ्र उठने और शीघ्र शान्त होने वाला होता है; वह श्याम या अरुण वर्ण का, या स्वाभाविक वर्ण का, चल, स्पन्दनयुक्त, खर, परुष और फटी त्वचा तथा रोमों वाला होता है; वह मानो काटा जाता है, मानो भेदा जाता है, मानो दबाया जाता है, मानो सुइयों से चुभोया जाता है, मानो उस पर चींटियाँ रेंगती हैं; मानो सरसों के कल्क से लिपा हुआ वह चिमचिमाता है, सिकुड़ता है और मानो खिंचता है: यह वातशोथ है।
english: But here is the specific feature: Vāta (vāyu), aggravated by cold, dry, light and non-slimy things, fatigue, fasting, excessive reduction, depletion and the like, overpowers the skin, flesh, blood and the rest and produces a swelling. It is quick to arise and quick to subside; it is dark or reddish in colour, or of natural colour; mobile, throbbing, with rough, harsh and split skin and hair; it is as if cut, as if split, as if pressed, as if pricked with needles, as if crept over by ants; as if smeared with mustard paste it tingles; it contracts and is as if stretched: this is the Vāta swelling.

text_flags.why: the avagraha after a visarga is out of place and 'sīta' is not a word; śīta (cold) heads the list of Vāta-aggravating qualities, cf. śīta in 7-3
ṛn (Devanagari वऋनो) is a typing error for varṇa (colour), cf. śyāmāruṇavarṇaḥ just before

notes: iti closes the description. chidyate etc. describe the swelling (or the sensation in it). cimicimāyate is an onomatopoeic verb for a tingling, prickling sensation.
lines_deva: अयं त्वत्र विशेषः ऽसीतरूक्षलघुविशदश्रमोपवासातिकर्शनक्षपणादिभिर्वायुः प्रकुपितस्त्वङ्मांसशोणितादीन्यभिभूय शोफं जनयति स क्षिप्रोत्थानप्रशमो भवति तथा श्यामारुणवर्णः प्रकृतिवऋनो वा चलः स्पन्दनः खरपरुषभिन्नत्वग्रोमा छिद्यत इव भिद्यत इव पीड्यत इव सूचीभिरिव तुद्यत इव पिपीलिकाभिरिव संसृप्यते सर्षपकल्कावलिप्त इव चिमिचिमायते संकुच्यत आयम्यत इवेति वातशोथः ;
lines_iast: ayaṃ tvatra viśeṣaḥ 'sītarūkṣalaghuviśadaśramopavāsātikarśanakṣapaṇādibhirvāyuḥ prakupitastvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitādīnyabhibhūya śophaṃ janayati sa kṣiprotthānapraśamo bhavati tathā śyāmāruṇavarṇaḥ prakṛtivaṛno vā calaḥ spandanaḥ kharaparuṣabhinnatvagromā chidyata iva bhidyata iva pīḍyata iva sūcībhiriva tudyata iva pipīlikābhiriva saṃsṛpyate sarṣapakalkāvalipta iva cimicimāyate saṃkucyata āyamyata iveti vātaśothaḥ ;

hindi: उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, कटु, क्षार, लवण, अम्ल भोजन और अजीर्ण में भोजन से तथा अग्नि और धूप के ताप से कुपित पित्त त्वचा, मांस और रक्त को अभिभूत करके शोथ उत्पन्न करता है। वह शीघ्र उठने और शीघ्र शान्त होने वाला होता है; काली, पीली, नीली या ताम्र आभा वाला, उष्ण, मृदु, कपिल या ताम्र वर्ण के रोमों वाला होता है; वह जलता है, दुखता है, धुआँ-सा उठता प्रतीत होता है, ऊष्मा छोड़ता है, पसीजता है, गीला होता है, और स्पर्श तथा उष्णता को सहन नहीं करता: यह पित्तशोथ है।
english: Pitta, aggravated by hot, sharp, pungent, alkaline, salty and sour foods and by eating during indigestion, and by the heat of fire and sun, overpowers the skin, flesh and blood and produces a swelling. It is quick to arise and quick to subside; it has a black, yellow, blue or coppery hue, is hot and soft, with tawny or coppery hair; it burns, smarts, feels as if fumigated, gives off heat, sweats and becomes moist, and does not tolerate touch or heat: this is the Pitta swelling.

text_flags.why: abhihbūya is not a form; abhibhūya as in 7-1 and 7-3
anusvāra before r and a missing ṛ (Devanagari ंर्दुः) is a typing error for mṛduḥ (soft)

possible: suṣūyata is no known form; the sense required is 'tolerates', the opposite of the Kapha swelling's sparśoṣṇasahaḥ ('tolerating touch and heat') in 7-3; mṛṣyate (√mṛṣ, to bear) is a conjecture only

notes: ajīrṇabhojana is read as 'eating during indigestion'; it could also be 'eating undigested (unwholesome) food'. The meaning of suṣūyata is taken from the contrast with 7-3; the verb itself is uncertain.

hindi: गुरु, मधुर, शीत, स्निग्ध पदार्थों से तथा अति निद्रा, व्यायाम न करने आदि से कुपित श्लेष्मा त्वचा, मांस, रक्त आदि को अभिभूत करके शोथ उत्पन्न करता है। वह कठिनाई से उठने और कठिनाई से शान्त होने वाला होता है; पाण्डु या श्वेत आभा वाला, गुरु, स्निग्ध, श्लक्ष्ण, स्थिर, घना, सफेद नोकों वाले रोमों वाला, और स्पर्श तथा उष्णता को सहने वाला होता है: यह श्लेष्मशोथ है।
english: Kapha (śleṣman), aggravated by heavy, sweet, cold and unctuous things and by excessive sleep, lack of exercise and the like, overpowers the skin, flesh, blood and the rest and produces a swelling. It arises and subsides with difficulty; it has a pale or white hue, is heavy, unctuous, smooth, firm and dense, with white-tipped hair, and tolerates touch and heat: this is the Kapha swelling.
lines_deva: गुरुमधुरशीतस्निग्धैरतिस्वप्नाव्यायामादिभिश्च श्लेष्मा प्रकुपितस्त्वङ्मांसशोणितादीन्यभिभूय शोथं जनयति स कृच्छ्रोत्थानप्रशमो भवति पाण्डुश्वेतावभासो गुरुः स्निग्धः श्लक्ष्णः स्थिरः स्त्यानः शुक्लाग्ररोमा स्पर्शोष्णसहश्चेति श्लेष्मशोथः;
lines_iast: gurumadhuraśītasnigdhairatisvapnāvyāyāmādibhiśca śleṣmā prakupitastvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitādīnyabhibhūya śothaṃ janayati sa kṛcchrotthānapraśamo bhavati pāṇḍuśvetāvabhāso guruḥ snigdhaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ sthiraḥ styānaḥ śuklāgraromā sparśoṣṇasahaśceti śleṣmaśothaḥ;

words.gloss: from the combination of their respective causes and forms
from the coming together of all their respective causes and forms
arising from all three doṣas together

hindi: अपने-अपने कारणों और आकृतियों के संसर्ग से द्विदोषज शोथ तीन होते हैं; अपने-अपने कारणों और आकृतियों के सन्निपात से सान्निपातिक शोथ एक होता है; इस प्रकार सात प्रकार का भेद है।
english: From the combination of their respective causes and forms, there are three swellings born of two doṣas; from the coming together of all their respective causes and forms, there is one sānnipātika [swelling] (from all three doṣas together); thus the division is sevenfold.
notes: The sevenfold count is three single-doṣa, three double-doṣa and one of all three.
lines_deva: यथास्वकारणाकृतिसंसर्गाद्द्विदोषजास्त्रयः शोथा भवन्ति यथास्वकारणाकृतिसन्निपातात् सान्निपातिक एकः; एवं सप्तविधो भेदः
lines_iast: yathāsvakāraṇākṛtisaṃsargāddvidoṣajāstrayaḥ śothā bhavanti yathāsvakāraṇākṛtisannipātāt sānnipātika ekaḥ; evaṃ saptavidho bhedaḥ

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. pass. part. √bhid

words.gloss: on account of the common feature of elevation

hindi: उन-उन प्रकृतियों से विभक्त होकर शोथ दो प्रकार का, तीन प्रकार का, चार प्रकार का, सात प्रकार का और आठ प्रकार का पाया जाता है; और फिर उत्सेध की समानता के कारण वह एक ही है।
english: Being divided according to these and those basic factors (prakṛti), swelling is found to be twofold, threefold, fourfold, sevenfold and eightfold; and again it is one alone, on account of the common feature of elevation (utsedha).

text_flags.why: the present passive participle of √bhid is bhidyamāna; bhidymāna is not a form
the word agrees with m. sg. śothaḥ (cf. dvividhaḥ, saptavidhaḥ); before s the visarga must stand, so caturvidhā is a typing error

notes: prakṛti here means the basic factors by which swellings are classified; the unit does not say which factors give each count. The repeated tābhis tābhiḥ is distributive ('these and those').
lines_deva: प्रकृतिभिस्ताभिस्ताभिर्भिद्य्मानो द्विविधस्त्रिविधश्चतुर्विधा सप्तविधोऽष्टविधश्च शोथ उपलभ्यते पुनश्चैक एवोत्सेधसामान्यात्
lines_iast: prakṛtibhistābhistābhirbhidymāno dvividhastrividhaścaturvidhā saptavidho'ṣṭavidhaśca śotha upalabhyate punaścaika evotsedhasāmānyāt

words.gram: n. nom. pl., past pass. part. √pīḍ

hindi: और यहाँ हैं: जिसके अङ्ग सूज जाते हैं, मानो सो जाते हैं और दुखते हैं, और दबाने पर शीघ्र ऊपर उठ आते हैं, उसे वातशोथ बताए।
english: And here there are: Whose limbs swell, are as if asleep and ache, and, when pressed, quickly rise up again: one should diagnose that as Vāta swelling.

text_flags.why: the 3 pl. present of ud-√nam is unnamanti (cf. nonnamati in 13); the long ā is a typing error
object of ādiśet, agreeing with tam: m. acc. sg. vātaśotham is required

notes: Line 1 is the lead-in formula 'bhavanti cātra'. tam (m.) refers to the swelling implied by the verse.
lines_deva: शूयन्ते यस्य गात्राणि स्वपन्तीव रुजन्ति च
lines_iast: śūyante yasya gātrāṇi svapantīva rujanti ca

hindi: और जो शोथ अरुण वर्ण की आभा वाला हो, रात में मिट जाए, और स्नेह-उष्णता तथा मर्दन से मिट जाए, वह भी वातिक है।
english: And the swelling which has a reddish hue, disappears at night, and would disappear with unctuous warmth and massage: that too is of Vāta nature (vātika).
notes: snehoṣṇamardanābhyām is dual: read as two means, 'unctuous warmth' (sneha-uṣṇa) and 'massage' (mardana); the dual excludes a single 'unctuous and warm massage'.
lines_deva: स्नेहोष्णमर्दनाभ्यां च प्रणश्येत् स च वातिकः
lines_iast: snehoṣṇamardanābhyāṃ ca praṇaśyet sa ca vātikaḥ

words.gloss: of one afflicted with thirst and fever

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past pass. part. √smṛ

hindi: प्यास और ज्वर से पीड़ित व्यक्ति का जो शोथ दुखता है, फिर जलता है, पसीजता है, गीला होता है और गन्धयुक्त होता है, वह पैत्त श्वयथु माना गया है।
english: The swelling of one afflicted with thirst and fever which smarts, then burns, sweats, becomes moist and has an odour is known as the Pitta swelling (śvayathu).

text_flags.why: the word for swelling is śvayathu (cf. śvayathuḥ in 15)

notes: gandhī is rendered literally 'having an odour'.
lines_deva: स्विद्यति क्लिद्यते गन्धी स पैत्तः श्वयतुः स्मृतः
lines_iast: svidyati klidyate gandhī sa paittaḥ śvayatuḥ smṛtaḥ

words.gloss: with yellow eyes, face and skin

hindi: जिस शोथ में आँखें, मुख और त्वचा पीले हों, जो पहले मध्य भाग से सूजे, जिसमें त्वचा पतली हो और अतिसार हो, वह पित्तशोथ कहा जाता है।
english: The swelling with yellow eyes, face and skin, which first swells from the middle, with thin skin and with diarrhoea: that is called the Pitta swelling.

text_flags.why: pitta has a double t (cf. pittaśothaḥ in 7-2)

notes: The bahuvrīhis (yellow eyes, face, skin; thin skin; atisārin) are grammatically attributes of the swelling, though they describe the patient. madhyāt 'from the middle' is taken as the middle of the body.
lines_deva: तनुत्वक् चातिसारी च पितशोथः स उच्यते
lines_iast: tanutvak cātisārī ca pitaśothaḥ sa ucyate

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past pass. part. ni-√pīḍ

hindi: किन्तु जो शोथ शीत, मन्द गति वाला, खुजली वाला और पाण्डु वर्ण का हो, और दबाने पर ऊपर न उठे, वह श्वयथु कफात्मक है।
english: But the swelling which is cold, slow in movement, itchy and pale, and, when pressed, does not rise up again: that swelling is of Kapha nature.

text_flags.why: kaṇḍū (itching) has retroflex ḍ, as in kaṇḍū in 6
the word for swelling is śvayathu (cf. 15)
the half-line has only 7 syllables; kaphātmakaḥ restores 8 and is the usual -ātmaka formation

notes: sakta-gati (literally 'whose movement is stuck') is rendered 'slow in movement', i.e. slow to spread.

words.gloss: from [it] cut with a knife or kuśa grass

hindi: जिस शोथ को शस्त्र या कुश से काटने पर उसमें से रक्त न बहे, और कठिनाई से चिपचिपी पिच्छा रिसे, वह भी कफ से उत्पन्न है।
english: The swelling from which, when it is cut with a knife or kuśa grass, blood does not flow, and slimy fluid (picchā) oozes with difficulty: that too arises from Kapha.

text_flags.why: pravatate is not a form; pra-√vṛt, pravartate (flows) gives the sense

notes: yasya (genitive) and chinnāt (ablative) both refer to the swelling: 'of which, from [it] when cut'.
lines_deva: कृच्छ्रेण पिच्छा स्रवति स चापि कफसंभवः
lines_iast: kṛcchreṇa picchā sravati sa cāpi kaphasaṃbhavaḥ

words.gloss: from the combination of causes and features

hindi: निदानों और आकृतियों के संसर्ग से श्वयथु द्विदोषज होता है; सन्निपात से सब आकृतियों वाला शोथ मिश्रित हेतुओं से उत्पन्न होता है।
english: From the combination of causes and features, a swelling is born of two doṣas; from sannipāta (the combination of all three), the swelling with all the features is born of mixed causes.

text_flags.why: smāsarga is not a word; saṃsarga (combination), as in kāraṇākṛtisaṃsargāt in 7

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past part. abhi-nir-√vṛt, tat-puruṣa
m. nom. sg., past part. pra-√sṛ

words.gloss: from the face of a woman

hindi: किन्तु जिस प्राणी का शोथ पैरों में उत्पन्न होकर सब अङ्गों में फैल जाए, वह बहुत कष्टदायक होता है; और वह भी जो स्त्री के मुख से फैला हो।
english: But the swelling of a person which, having arisen in the feet, spreads to all the limbs, is very grave; and so is that which has spread from the face in a woman.

text_flags.why: missing vowel: yaḥ tu (cf. yastu in 13)
bhavaet is not a form; optative bhavet

notes: strīmukhāt is read as 'from a woman's face', i.e. a swelling in a woman that starts in the face and spreads.
lines_deva: जन्तोः स च सुकष्टः स्यात् प्रसृतः स्त्रीमुखाच्च यः
lines_iast: jantoḥ sa ca sukaṣṭaḥ syāt prasṛtaḥ strīmukhācca yaḥ

hindi: और जो शोथ स्त्री या पुरुष के गुह्य भाग में उत्पन्न हो, वह भी सबसे अधिक कष्टदायक जानना चाहिए, और वह भी जिसमें उपद्रव हों।
english: And that which arises in the genitals, of a woman or of a man, is to be known as the gravest; and so is that in which there are complications.
notes: striyā is the genitive striyāḥ with the visarga dropped before v by sandhi, parallel to puruṣasya.
lines_deva: यश्चापि गुह्यप्रभवः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा
स च कष्टतमो ज्ञेयो यस्य च स्युरुपद्रवाः
lines_iast: yaścāpi guhyaprabhavaḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā
sa ca kaṣṭatamo jñeyo yasya ca syurupadravāḥ

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (lengthened form of atisāra)

words.gloss: summary of the complications of swelling

hindi: छर्दि, श्वास, अरुचि, तृष्णा, ज्वर और अतिसार: दुर्बलता के साथ यह सप्तक शोथ के उपद्रवों का संग्रह है।
english: Vomiting, dyspnoea, loss of taste, thirst, fever and diarrhoea: this set of seven, with weakness, is the summary of the complications of swelling.

text_flags.why: upadrava (complication), cf. upadravāḥ in 17; upadarava gives the half-line 9 syllables instead of 8

notes: Six items are listed; weakness (daurbalya) makes the seventh.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

words.gloss: at the root of the tongue

hindi: जिसका कुपित श्लेष्मा जिह्वा के मूल में ठहर जाता है और शीघ्र शोथ उत्पन्न करता है, उसे उपजिह्विका होती है।
english: In whom aggravated Kapha (śleṣman) settles at the root of the tongue and quickly produces a swelling, in him upajihvikā arises.

text_flags.why: object of saṃjanayet: m. acc. sg. śotham, as śophaṃ in the same position in 20 to 22

notes: Disease name upajihvikā kept in Sanskrit. The optative saṃjanayet is rendered as a plain present.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

words.gloss: in the kākala (part of the throat)

hindi: जिसका कुपित श्लेष्मा काकल में ठहर जाता है, वह शीघ्र शोफ उत्पन्न करके गलशुण्डिका कर देता है।
english: In whom aggravated Kapha (śleṣman) settles in the kākala, it quickly produces a swelling and causes galaśuṇḍikā.
notes: kākala and the disease name galaśuṇḍikā are kept in Sanskrit; kākala is a part of the throat.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

words.gloss: on the outside of the throat

hindi: जिसका कुपित श्लेष्मा गले के बाहरी भाग में ठहर जाता है और धीरे-धीरे शोफ उत्पन्न करता है, उसे गलगण्ड होता है।
english: In whom aggravated Kapha (śleṣman) settles on the outside of the throat and slowly produces a swelling, in him galagaṇḍa arises.
notes: Disease name galagaṇḍa kept in Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup
m. loc. sg., compound with ind. antar

hindi: जिसका कुपित श्लेष्मा गले के भीतर स्थिर होकर ठहरता है और शीघ्र शोफ उत्पन्न करता है, उसे गलग्रह होता है।
english: In whom aggravated Kapha (śleṣman) stays fixed inside the throat and quickly produces a swelling, in him galagraha arises.

text_flags.why: possible: the final t of saṃjanayet before ś should appear as c (cch), as in 20 and 21

notes: Disease name galagraha kept in Sanskrit. antargale is taken as loc. 'inside the throat'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

hindi: जिसका कुपित पित्त रक्त के साथ त्वचा में फैलता है और लालिमायुक्त शोफ उत्पन्न करता है, उसे विसर्प होता है।
english: In whom aggravated Pitta spreads in the skin together with blood and produces a reddened swelling, in him visarpa arises.

text_flags.why: transposed letters; yasya as in every verse of this group
agrees with n. pittam (cf. pittaṃ prakupitaṃ in 24 and 27)
sarpapi is not a form; 3 sg. pres. sarpati (spreads), which fits visarpa
agrees with m. acc. śopham (cf. śothaṃ sarāgaṃ in 24)

notes: Disease name visarpa kept in Sanskrit.
lines_deva: यसय् पित्तं प्रकुपिता सरक्तं त्वचि सर्पपि
lines_iast: yasay pittaṃ prakupitā saraktaṃ tvaci sarpapi

words.gram: n. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

hindi: जिसका कुपित पित्त त्वचा और रक्त में ठहर जाता है और लालिमायुक्त शोथ उत्पन्न करता है, उसे पिडका होती है।
english: In whom aggravated Pitta settles in the skin and blood and produces a reddened swelling, in him piḍakā (eruption) arises.
notes: piḍakā may be singular or a collective; rendered as the disease name. tvaci rakte has no 'and' in the text; it may also mean 'in the blood in the skin'.
lines_deva: शोथं सरागं जनयेत् पिडका तस्य जायते
lines_iast: śothaṃ sarāgaṃ janayet piḍakā tasya jāyate

words.gram: n. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

hindi: जिसका कुपित पित्त रक्त में पहुँचकर सूख जाता है, उसे तिलक, पिप्लु, व्यङ्ग और नीलिका होते हैं।
english: In whom aggravated Pitta, reaching the blood, dries up, in him tilakas, piplus, vyaṅgas and nīlikā arise.

text_flags.why: possible: before p the visarga of the m. nom. pl. should stand (tilakāḥ piplavaḥ)

notes: Disease names tilaka, piplu, vyaṅga and nīlikā kept in Sanskrit. The singular verb jāyate agrees with the nearest subject nīlikā.
lines_deva: यस्य प्रकुपितं पित्तं शोणितं प्राप्य शुष्यति
तिलका पिप्लवो व्यङ्गा नीलिका तस्य जायते
lines_iast: yasya prakupitaṃ pittaṃ śoṇitaṃ prāpya śuṣyati
tilakā piplavo vyaṅgā nīlikā tasya jāyate

words.gram: n. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

hindi: जिसका कुपित पित्त दोनों शङ्खों में ठहर जाता है, उसे शङ्खक नाम का दारुण श्वयथु होता है।
english: In whom aggravated Pitta settles in the temples, in him a dreadful swelling named śaṅkhaka arises.

text_flags.why: agrees with n. pittam (cf. 24, 27)
transposed letters; śvayathu as in 15

notes: Disease name śaṅkhaka kept in Sanskrit; śaṅkha (dual) = the temples.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., past part. pra-√kup

words.gloss: at the root of the ear

hindi: जिसका कुपित पित्त कान के मूल में ठहर जाता है, उसे ज्वर के अन्त में दुर्जय और अन्त की ओर ले जाने वाला शोथ उत्पन्न होता है।
english: In whom aggravated Pitta settles at the root of the ear, in him, at the end of a fever, a swelling arises that is hard to overcome and leads to the end.
notes: antāya (dative of anta, 'end') means 'for the end', i.e. leading to death.
